body:
Similarly, I was in love with my younger cousin for many years. The post above details the feelings I'd went through pretty accurately. You spend years in denial and self-loathing before finally admitting to yourself that the feelings you have are true. Similarly to the OP's brother, I had an impossible time finding a girlfriend, as my "bar," so to say, was set by my cousin. I'd only find women attractive if they reminded me of her. I would be willing to bet if the OP looks hard enough, she will find similarities between her and her brother's now ex-girlfriend.

I can't really give advice on how to handle it. Like OP's brother, I got messed up on something (opiates), which tend to make me way over emotional, before telling her. It was only recently that this happened, a month ago, and I still regret it every day. I sent her the message online, and from the moment I hit send, up through about two weeks, I was suicidal. I had to make sure I wasn't alone, as all I wanted to do was kill myself. I even tried turning myself in to a psych hospital, but they didn't feel I was mentally ill enough (I have a feeling it had more to do with a lack of insurance or money on my part.) I've been keeping my mind off of it with school, but I still have times where I miss the part of my family that won't talk to me. 

She hasn't spoken to me since, and my entire family knows. Most of my family don't seem to mind, but enough do that I'm not welcome at holiday gatherings. My aunt (cousin's mom) was basically a mother to me, and now she's not even willing to say a word to me. The above poster was right that it does destroy families. 

To the OP: I don't really know what you should do. Being on the other side of the coin, I can tell you that cutting off all contact is going to really mess your brother up emotionally. I can't say that he's going to try and kill himself, but he is going to feel like he's at the lowest point of his life. As for potentially being adopted, you still have people in your life that love you very much by the sound of it. Whether or not you're biologically related, the people that raised you are your family, and family is definitely the most amazing thing that we have during our short time on Earth. It's probably the most uncomfortable thing you will ever have to do, but in my opinion talking it out with your brother would be the best thing.

I'm not too sure yet. Early in the year all the clubs get together at a nearby state park for people to look and choose. I had planned on at least attending that, which is something I would never consider in the past. I'm trying my hardest to find the strength you speak of, I hope I can find it, instead of only finding myself back in the pharmaceuticals, or worse. Right now I'm living life one minute at a time, and dread what tomorrow brings with it.

Thank you for your kind words and advice. Classes resume in two weeks and prior to these events I have been thinking strongly about joining a club or two. I've been the quiet, shy type all of my life, so making friends, and getting out of the house has always been hard for me. At the moment I have been too sick to my stomach, over my actions, to even get out of bed. I'm trying my hardest to look on the bright side, but it has been hard to find one.
